importFormats.about: Batch 22: the transaction exports a coach drops into SLAM at month end. Each format is recognized by its header row (detect: every one of these headers is there, any order, any case). columns: the header row as the app writes it. roles: which column is which. sign: out-positive means money out is a positive number (it is turned around on the way in), out-negative means money out is negative. The generic bank CSV has no fixed header: the date, description and amount (or debit and credit) columns are guessed from the header words, and asked for when they cannot be.
importFormats.source: Rocket Money: Transactions, Export (help article) and the header row of an export; Monarch: Settings, Data, Download transactions (help articles and two converters that read the file). Links per format.

formats.name: Rocket Money
formats.how: Rocket Money on the web: Transactions, Export, Export again; the file comes by email (Download File).
formats.signNote: Spending is written as a positive amount; the direction is checked against the Income rows in the file and kept as is when they say otherwise.
formats.checked: The help article gives the steps but not the columns; the header row is the one Rocket Money writes (Account Name, Account Number, Institution Name, Name, Custom Name are named in the converter linked here). A coach who sees a different header: the file falls back to the generic bank CSV.

formats.checked: Date, Merchant, Category, Account, Original Statement, Notes, Amount, Tags in this order (both converters); Owner on household plans.

importCategories.about: Batch 22: how each app's own category names land on SLAM's Budget categories (the category on a Budget line). A name maps to a line category, or to @income (money in), @transfer (between the client's own accounts or a card payment, kept out of spending), @debt (a loan or card payment, kept out of spending and marked Paid on the calendar), @ignore (left out) or null (not matched: the coach picks). A coach can change any of these for one client on the import review; that change is kept with the client (settings.importCategoryMap).
importCategories.source: Monarch: Default Categories (help article); Rocket Money: Internal Transfers and Credit Card Payment from the help article on transfers, the other names as they appear in an export. Matched to SLAM categories by the coach rule (Eli, Nov 6 2026: keep tracking in Rocket Money or Monarch, bring the month in).

merchantWords.about: Batch 22: the last step of matching. Words in a transaction's merchant or description (lower case, whole words or the start of one) and the Budget line category they point to. A Budget line's own name counts too (a line called Rent catches RENT PAYMENT). kind: paycheck or transfer instead of a category keeps the row out of spending. A match from these words is shown as Guessed.
merchantWords.source: SLAM rule (Eli, Nov 6 2026): common US merchants, made up for matching, not a list from any app

fireDrill.about: Batch 44 (M9F, js/math/firedrill.js): the bank fire drill. order is the order to pay in when not everything can be paid, first to last (childcare beside getting to work, QUESTIONS 365); each tier lists the Budget categories, DRAFTT letters, debt types and calendar kinds it holds, and card says whether a credit card can usually pay it (not rent, not another debt).
fireDrill.source: CFPB, Your Money, Your Goals: Prioritizing bills (files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_ymyg_behind-on-bills_print.pdf: stay housed and keep utilities connected, keep the job, then other loans and credit cards) and CFPB, Tools to help when you can't pay your bills (Apr 17 2020: cover food, housing, utilities and phone first); the NFCC counselors' order (keep the roof, the heat, the car you work from and the food before the debts), via the older suite's data/bill_triage.json (Sep 6 2026). Childcare sits beside getting to work, ahead of health: both keep the paycheck coming (QUESTIONS 365, Nov 6 2026; the older suite put childcare needed for work with housing). Checked Nov 6 2026

order.label: Housing
order.call: Your landlord or mortgage servicer, before the due date: ask for a few days or a payment plan. A HUD-approved housing counselor is free (hud.gov).

order.label: Utilities and phone
order.call: The utility: ask for a payment arrangement. 211 knows local help with energy bills.

order.label: Food
order.call: 211 or a food bank. Using one while an account is sorted out is what it is for.

order.label: Getting to work and childcare
order.call: The car lender: ask to move one payment to the end of the loan. The daycare or sitter: ask for a few days; a state child care assistance office (childcare.gov) can help.

order.label: Health
order.call: The provider or the plan: ask to change the payment date.

order.label: Minimum payments
order.call: The card or loan company: ask for its hardship program by name. A nonprofit counselor at nfcc.org is free.

order.label: Tax payments
order.call: The IRS: a short payment plan can be set up online.

order.label: Everything else
order.call: Pause it, or move its date, until the account is sorted out.

unclaimed.how: Old deposits, refunds and final paychecks go to the state when a business cannot reach you. MissingMoney (run with NAUPA, the state treasurers' unclaimed property group) searches most states at once; unclaimed.org links each state's own site.
